currentState: Chapter 7: Corin is formal and careful with her ('Ranger-General', all of it); Sylvanas gives him no name aloud and a single grudging note in her head: the Dalaran boy has been right every time he opened his mouth. She tests him once in thought (a patient man with the keys to the inspection office could as easily be sitting on bills for somebody else) and sets it aside; she lets his speed carry the argument against Havel and tells him to stay behind Proudmoore.
powerDynamic: Sylvanas commands; Corin offers and does not push. She uses him as the carrier of paper and access.

physicalDynamics.pattern: Corin turns a waybill round to face her and puts an inky finger by the hook; brings out Kett's bills without looking for them; stands with the satchel buckled on the second try; Sylvanas pinches the candle out on her last order to him.

nameUsage.sylvanasCallsCorin: No name aloud ('Take him.', 'Stay behind Proudmoore.'); interior 'the boy', 'the Dalaran boy'.

history.event: Chapter 7: Sylvanas 'Take him.' (to Jaina, of Corin) at the bench; at the post she questions Corin's figures with short questions ('How many?').
Chapter 7: Sylvanas holds a grudge against Havel for slowness and finds the Dalaran boy right every time; Corin volunteers for the raid; Sylvanas tells him to stay behind Proudmoore.

trajectory: Ch7: the boy earns his place by being right and moving toward the danger.
